title: When a metabolizing enzyme variant matters

segs.text: Section eight. When a metabolizing enzyme variant matters. Variation in metabolizing enzymes is the biggest reason for variation in drug response. A variant is clinically important in three cases: the enzyme is the major route that eliminates the drug or ends its action; the drug is a prodrug, given inactive, that an enzyme must activate; or an altered pathway, or the parent drug itself, causes toxicity. A drug excreted unchanged by the kidney does not depend on a metabolizing enzyme, so a variant there does not change how it is handled.

The direction of harm depends on whether the drug is already active or a prodrug. A poor metabolizer cannot run the enzyme step, so an active drug is not removed and climbs toward toxicity, while a prodrug is never turned on and fails. An ultrarapid metabolizer runs the step too fast, so an active drug is gone before it works, and a prodrug is over activated, which can overdose the patient.

Clopidogrel shows that the busiest enzyme is not always the one that decides. It is a platelet receptor inhibitor, which stops platelets sticking together, and a prodrug. About eighty five percent of a dose is inactivated by esterases and only about fifteen percent is activated in two C Y P steps, yet variants in C Y P two C nineteen most change how much active drug forms.
